question: Lactulose achieves its laxative effect primarily through which mechanism?

answers.text: It is a non-absorbable disaccharide that retains water in the colon osmotically and is fermented by colonic bacteria to short-chain fatty acids that further draw water into the lumen

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Lactulose is neither hydrolysed by intestinal enzymes nor absorbed. In the colon, bacteria ferment it to lactic acid, acetic acid, and CO₂, creating an osmotic and acidic environment that draws water into the lumen and softens stool.

answers.text: It directly stimulates myenteric plexus neurons to increase colonic propulsive contractions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Direct myenteric stimulation is the mechanism of stimulant laxatives such as senna (sennosides) and bisacodyl — a mechanistically different class. Lactulose has no direct effect on enteric nerves.

answers.text: It inhibits water absorption by blocking the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase in colonic epithelial cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Lactulose does not act on colonic ion transporters. Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase inhibition is not a laxative mechanism; drugs like ricinoleic acid (castor oil metabolite) affect epithelial permeability but through a different mechanism.

answers.text: It forms a viscous gel in the small intestine that slows absorption and increases stool bulk like a dietary fibre

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Gel-forming viscous bulk is the mechanism of bulk-forming agents such as psyllium (ispaghula husk) and methylcellulose — a different laxative class. Lactulose reaches the colon largely unchanged and works by osmotic action.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the osmotic laxative section. Lactulose is non-absorbed and non-hydrolysed — it works in the colon via osmosis and bacterial fermentation, not via nerve stimulation or bulk formation.

Well done. Lactulose exemplifies osmotic laxative pharmacology: it reaches the colon undigested, creates osmotic and fermentation-derived acidity, and draws water — a mechanism safe even in chronic use.
